ap_microeconomics-f01.title: A market with a price ceiling

stimulus.description: Quantity demanded and quantity supplied of bottled water at different prices in a competitive market.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the competitive market for bottled water. On your graph, label the equilibrium price (P_E) and the equilibrium quantity (Q_E).
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. A downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve with Price and Quantity axes, intersecting at P_E and Q_E.

required_elements: Draws a downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve with Price and Quantity labeled on the axes and the curves labeled
alt_solutions: curves may be labeled D and S
axes may be labeled P and Q
common_errors: draws two curves with the same slope sign
omits an axis label
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels the intersection of the curves as the equilibrium with P_E on the price axis and Q_E on the quantity axis
alt_solutions: drops dashed lines from the intersection to the axes
labels the equilibrium point E with P_E and Q_E
common_errors: labels a point that is not the intersection
labels only the price
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Using the table, determine the equilibrium quantity.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied at $15, where 60 units are traded.

required_elements: Identifies the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied and reads the quantity (the quantity answer is correct)
alt_solutions: the row where the two quantities are equal
equilibrium quantity from the table
common_errors: reports the equilibrium price instead of the quantity
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The government sets a price ceiling of $12 per unit. On your graph, show the price ceiling, label the quantity actually traded (Q_C), and label the shortage.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. A horizontal line at the ceiling below P_E, Q_C on the quantity axis at the quantity supplied at the ceiling, and the horizontal gap between supply and demand at the ceiling labeled as the shortage.

required_elements: Draws a horizontal price ceiling line below the equilibrium price and labels it with the ceiling price
alt_solutions: the line may extend across the graph at the ceiling price
the line is labeled price ceiling or PC
common_errors: draws the ceiling above the equilibrium price
draws a vertical line
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels Q_C where the ceiling meets the supply curve and marks the gap between the supply and demand curves at the ceiling as the shortage
alt_solutions: Q_C is marked on the horizontal axis at the quantity supplied
the shortage is shown as a horizontal segment between supply and demand
common_errors: marks Q_C at the quantity demanded
labels the surplus instead of the shortage
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Using the table, calculate the quantity demanded and the quantity supplied at the price ceiling and the size of the shortage.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. At $12: quantity demanded is 72 and quantity supplied is 51, so the shortage is 21 units.

required_elements: Reads the quantity demanded and quantity supplied at the ceiling price (both answers are correct)
alt_solutions: row of the table at the ceiling price
quantity demanded and supplied at the ceiling
common_errors: reads quantities at the equilibrium price
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Subtracts quantity supplied from quantity demanded to find the shortage (the shortage answer is correct)
alt_solutions: difference between demanded and supplied
excess of quantity demanded over quantity supplied
common_errors: reports the quantity traded as the shortage
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Explain why the price ceiling creates a deadweight loss.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. The quantity traded falls below the efficient quantity, so some transactions in which the buyer's value exceeds the seller's cost do not occur, which lowers total surplus and creates a deadweight loss.

required_elements: States that the quantity traded under the ceiling is less than the equilibrium (efficient) quantity
alt_solutions: fewer units are bought and sold than at equilibrium
the quantity traded is limited by the quantity supplied at the ceiling
common_errors: says the quantity traded rises
says the quantity traded equals the quantity demanded
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains the lost mutually beneficial trades
required_elements: Explains that some transactions in which buyers value the good above its cost of production do not occur, so total surplus falls (the deadweight loss)
alt_solutions: trades where willingness to pay exceeds the cost are lost
total surplus is lower than at the equilibrium
common_errors: says total surplus rises
says producers gain more than consumers lose
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: F
parts.prompt: Suppose instead the government had set a price ceiling of $18 per unit. Identify what would happen to the quantity traded and explain why.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. The quantity traded would not change, because $18 is above the equilibrium price of $15, so the ceiling is not binding.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the ceiling is nonbinding and gives the reason
required_elements: States that the quantity traded would be unchanged because a ceiling above the equilibrium price is not binding
alt_solutions: no effect on price or quantity
the market stays at equilibrium
common_errors: says a shortage would arise
says the quantity traded would fall
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

ap_microeconomics-f02.title: Comparative advantage and gains from trade

stimulus.description: Maximum output per day if a country uses all of its resources to produce only one good.

notes: Each country's opportunity cost is constant, so each country's production possibilities curve is a straight line.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the opportunity cost of producing one unit of laptops, in units of chairs, in each country.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Country A: 12/36 = 0.33 units of chairs; Country B: 30/15 = 2.00 units of chairs.

required_elements: Divides the amount of the other good given up by the amount of this good gained for Country A (the answer is correct)
alt_solutions: units of the other good per unit of this good
ratio of the maximum outputs
common_errors: inverts the ratio
reports the maximum output of the other good
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Divides the amount of the other good given up by the amount of this good gained for Country B (the answer is correct)
alt_solutions: units of the other good per unit of this good
ratio of the maximum outputs
common_errors: inverts the ratio
reports the maximum output of the other good
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Which country has the comparative advantage in producing laptops? Identify the country.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Country A, because its opportunity cost of laptops is lower.

required_elements: Identifies the country with the lower opportunity cost of the good as the one with the comparative advantage
alt_solutions: the country that gives up less of the other good
Country A has the lower cost
common_errors: picks the country with the larger absolute output
picks the country with the higher opportunity cost
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Explain why both countries can gain if Country A exports laptops to Country B at a price of 1.17 units of chairs per unit of laptops.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. The price of 1.17 is above Country A's opportunity cost (0.33) and below Country B's (2.00), so each country obtains the good for less than it would cost to produce at home.

required_elements: Explains that the trading price lies between the two opportunity costs, so each country obtains the good at a cost lower than its own opportunity cost
alt_solutions: each country gets the good for less than it gives up at home
the price is between the two opportunity costs
common_errors: says only the exporter gains
says trade benefits only the country with the absolute advantage
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled production possibilities curve for Country A with laptops on the horizontal axis. Label the maximum quantity of each good.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. A straight line from 12 units of chairs on the vertical axis to 36 units of laptops on the horizontal axis.

required_elements: Draws a downward-sloping PPC with both axes labeled and the intercepts labeled with the maximum quantity of each good for Country A
alt_solutions: the curve may be a straight line because the opportunity cost is constant
intercepts may be marked with the numbers from the table
common_errors: swaps the axis intercepts
draws an upward-sloping curve
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

stimulus.description: Price and quantity demanded of pizza before and after a price increase.

notes: In a separate study of a different market, a 4 percent increase in the price of pizza caused the quantity demanded of salad to fall by 6 percent.

parts.prompt: Using the midpoint method, calculate the absolute value of the price elasticity of demand for pizza between the two prices.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Percentage change in quantity = 13.3%, percentage change in price = 9.5%, elasticity = 1.40.

required_elements: Computes the percentage change in quantity and in price using midpoints as the base (both are correct)

stimulus.description: Payoff matrix for two firms, Airline X (rows) and Airline Y (columns), each choosing to high fare or low fare. The firms choose simultaneously, once, with no binding agreement. Payoffs are profits in millions of dollars, listed as (Airline X, Airline Y).

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Does Airline X have a dominant strategy? If so, identify it and justify using the payoffs.
parts.model_answer: Yes: low fare. Whatever Airline Y chooses, Airline X earns more with low fare (for example 100 vs 73 if Airline Y chooses high fare, and 51 vs 36 if Airline Y chooses low fare).

required_elements: Names the strategy that pays the firm more against every choice of the rival (its dominant strategy)

choosing low fare is always better for Airline X

says there is no dominant strategy

better regardless of what the other firm does

justifies with the highest total payoff
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains that at least one firm has an incentive to deviate from that outcome (a better response exists), so it is not stable
required_elements: Explains that a firm can earn more by deviating from that outcome, so it is not stable without enforcement
alt_solutions: a firm can earn more by deviating
the dominant strategy tempts a firm away
cheating pays
common_errors: says the outcome is infeasible because payoffs are lower
says firms are irrational
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

blueprint.subject: ap_microeconomics
blueprint.concept: Dominant strategy, Nash equilibrium, and a mutually better outcome in a two-firm game
student_thinking: Compare each firm's payoffs holding the rival's choice fixed to find a dominant strategy
Find the strategy pair where neither firm benefits from deviating
Compare equilibrium payoffs with the other outcomes and explain the incentive problem

key_conditions.condition: Simultaneous one-shot game with the payoffs shown and no enforceable agreement

verification.independent_path: best-response enumeration cross-checked by a separate Nash/dominance module (micro_checks.nash)
